To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The emergence of the new educational executives is not a new development, but a continuation of a long-term historical trend; (2) This trend has roots in a variety of structural and political shifts in American education, including the rise of the federal government as an actor in the educational system; and (3) The new educational executives are a product of these shifts, and are not simply a result of particular individuals or specific circumstances.
the new executives' involvement in education is not new, but a continuation of the historic involvement of governors and mayors in education.
the emergence of the so-called new educational executives grows out of structural changes in the institutional landscape that have reabsorbed educational politics into general purpose governance.
